checks_run.procedure: Challenge the documented D-077 residual with my own probe r17-identity-residual.mjs. A opens Transformations through the nav (the /me fires); B is signed into the same cookie jar 70-90 ms later. R1: toggle 'Include archived' inside the 2 s window (search parameter only), then search a never-fetched term after the window. R2: navigate inside the window.
checks_run.command: node rv/r17-identity-residual.mjs (stack-run-4 attempt 1, stack-run-5 attempt 2, stack-run-6 attempt 3; also stack-run-7 and -8 with default limits)
checks_run.environment: Node 24.21.0, Chromium, fresh stacks; raised and default limits
checks_run.expected: Navigations inside the window switch to B at once. The next uncached GET after the window asks /me first and shows B. The inside-window filter is the documented residual: an observation, judged for disclosure.
checks_run.actual: Attempt 3: 5/5 with raised limits (stack-run-6) and 5/5 with default limits (stack-run-7 and stack-run-8). R2 asks /me (meGETs=2), and the timeline is A1 (A's own screen, first sample) then B0 throughout: B's name, no A record. R1 after the window: meFirst=true, header B. R1 inside the window (OBS): header A, list GET under B's cookie ('no transformations match', A's New transformation button), meGETs=0. That reproduces the documented residual exactly. I accept it as bounded and non-disclosing: the data is the current cookie holder's own, signed in from the same browser; nothing of A reaches B; writes carry A's CSRF token. Attempt 1 exited 1 on a probe mistake: Playwright check() threw 'Clicking the checkbox did not change its state' because the checkbox is URL-driven, and no assertion ran. Attempt 2 exited 1 with 2 FAIL lines (en/ar.R1.after-window), also a probe mistake: unticking returned to a still-fresh cached list, so no GET was sent (listGETs=0) and the screen showed A's own cached list under A's own header. Both attempts are kept with their probes. stack-run-4 and -5 EXIT=1 come solely from these attempts.
